name: Manasseh
overview: Manasseh was the firstborn son of Joseph and Asenath, born in Egypt before the years of famine (Genesis 41:50, 46:20). Joseph named him Manasseh, meaning 'Forgetting,' because God helped him forget all his toil and his father's house (Genesis 41:51). On his deathbed, Jacob adopted Manasseh and his brother Ephraim as his own sons, granting them a status equal to Reuben and Simeon among the tribes of Israel (Genesis 48:1, 5). The blessings pronounced upon Manasseh affirm God's provision and favor, promising heavenly and earthly blessings through the God of their father (Genesis 49:25).
